analysis: Both changed files are test-only. SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift changes only a comment near line 4361, clarifying that SSDWriteBehind.consume charges per entry in array order when a donation does not fit. The new SSDWriteBehindLedgerChargeTests.swift adds tests for the rolling-day write ledger (.write-budget) charging. They cover a single summed charge per donation, a fallback to per-block charging when the ledger is busy, and writing the leading blocks that fit near the daily or shared cap. The helper uses flock on the ledger file and test-local temp directories under SSDTestDirectory.parent(). It touches no production code, keys, attestation or network paths, and I saw no secrets in it. The tests exercise endurance controls related to T-041 and T-016 (disk and wear). They do not alter at-rest crypto, HMAC lookup names, TTL, the salt scoping or the other T-041 mitigations. The production change that these tests imply (a single ledger charge per donation in SSDWriteBehind and SSDWriteRateLimiter) is not in the supplied units, so I could not review its implementation. Unreviewed questions are whether a busy-ledger fallback fails closed, so that it cannot bypass the daily write cap, and whether the summed charge could under-count. The tests pin the fail-closed and cap behaviour (writeRateLimited counts, ledger exhaustion at the exact cost), which is reassuring. No security regression or threat-model gap is identified in the supplied changes.
